title: Escalate the planner's model and effort when planning thrashes
summary: When a plan is sent back for another try (a critic revise, or a mechanical plan-rule revision), the next planner call runs with the configured hard producer model and effort instead of the ordinary ones. First attempts are unchanged. The audience is the owner running Athena, who wants planning thrash fixed by a stronger model rather than by repeating the same call.

defaults_applied.how: New unit tests; cargo test and clippy criteria.
Criteria check the recorded planner model and effort per round, not that wiring exists.
One focused change in the planner call path.
Docs and changelog entry written for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: I read crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs. plan_round loops rounds 1..=max_rounds, and inside each round planning_round runs again after a mechanical finding (MAX_MECHANICAL_PASSES = 2). The planner spec uses ctx.reading.producer_model and the default effort. I also read crates/athena-core/src/run/producer.rs, which overrides spec.effort from reading.producer_effort, crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, which calls Models::producer_setting(model, hard), and crates/athena-data/src/config.rs, where Models has hard_producer_model and hard_producer_effort. No records file or data file is added under crates/, so check_record_file and AnyRecord are not touched.

Existing code: the change reuses Models::producer_setting in crates/athena-data/src/config.rs and the spec.effort override pattern in crates/athena-core/src/run/producer.rs. It adds no new config keys.

Reading of the request: 'thrashing' means a plan that was sent back for revision (round > 1 or mechanical_passes > 0). 'Increase intelligence / improve the model' means using the existing hard producer model and effort for the planner, and only when hard_producer_model or hard_producer_effort is configured. If neither is set, behaviour is unchanged.
The critic is not escalated. Only the planner is, because it is the role that thrashes on revision.
No change to athena.toml or defaults.toml: the existing hard_producer_* keys are the settings used. If the repository config sets none, the owner sets them separately.
crates/athena-core/src/status/planning.rs and every figure status prints are not changed. The change does not alter any records measure computation, so no real-records range check applies.
This is not a new or tightened refusal rule, so no refusal-rate criterion applies.

acceptance_criteria.text: In crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs, the planner AgentSpec built in planning_round takes its model and effort from Models::producer_setting(.., true) when round > 1 or mechanical_passes > 0. Round 1, pass 0 keeps the current model and effort. The diff shows both branches.

A new unit test in crates/athena-core/src/run/ (using the fake agent) shows that the first planner invocation records the ordinary model and effort and that the planner invocation after a critic revise records hard_producer_model and hard_producer_effort. Run `cargo test -p athena-core` and cite the test name.

A new test shows that a mechanical plan-rule revision also escalates the next planner call, and that with no hard_producer_* configured the planner model and effort stay the same on every round. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.

The planner escalation is visible to the owner: the planner line printed by planning_round, or the invocation record, shows the escalated model, so a run's output can be checked. Exercise it with `cargo test -p athena-cli` using the fake agent.
cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets and cargo test --workspace pass. Name each as its own simple command, or cite the Athena-recorded passing checks on the final tree.

CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the change. Docs that describe planning (docs/spec.toml or the planning docs) say that a revised plan runs the planner at the hard setting. docs/decisions.md gets a new appended decision with a Provenance bullet, and no existing entry is edited.

out_of_scope: Escalating the critic, reader or verifier.
Changing athena.toml, defaults.toml or any other governance file.
Changing crates/athena-core/src/status/planning.rs or any records measure.
Adding new config keys or new retry limits.
departures: Slightly higher cost and time than the reference: it needs fake-agent tests across the revise loop and touches the pipeline.
urgent_reason: It cuts wasted time from planning thrash: repeated planner revise rounds and plan-rule retries that end in a stopped job.
hard_reason: It changes the run pipeline: how the planner stage is called inside the plan/critic revision loop, and which model and effort it gets.
